title: Wayland: pen barrel button BTN_STYLUS is reported as MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT, the same as the pen tip
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf].
- The same mapping is in `master` as of 2026-10-01, `platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp`, `WaylandThread::_wp_tablet_tool_on_button`.

### System information

Fedora Linux 44 (Workstation), GNOME Shell / mutter 50.5, libinput 1.31.3, Wayland display driver (`--display-driver wayland`), Wacom Intuos Pro M (056a:0357) with its Pro Pen

### Issue description

On the Wayland display server, one of the pen's two barrel buttons (`BTN_STYLUS`) reaches Godot as `MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT`, the same event the pen tip sends on contact. So a project cannot tell that barrel button from the tip, and cannot bind it to anything. `BTN_STYLUS3` and any other tool button are dropped.

The handler maps the codes like this:

```cpp
if (button == BTN_STYLUS) {
	mouse_button = MouseButton::LEFT;
}

if (button == BTN_STYLUS2) {
	mouse_button = MouseButton::RIGHT;
}
```

The compositor sends the raw evdev codes on `zwp_tablet_tool_v2.button`. `WAYLAND_DEBUG=client` shows `331` (`BTN_STYLUS`) for one barrel button and `332` (`BTN_STYLUS2`) for the other. In GNOME, the per-stylus button mapping in Settings is not applied for a `tablet-v2` client, so the mapping above is the only one a Godot project ever sees.

GTK maps the same codes to middle, right and back (`gdk/wayland/gdkseat-wayland.c`, `tablet_tool_handle_button`):

```c
if (button == BTN_STYLUS)
  n_button = GDK_BUTTON_MIDDLE;
else if (button == BTN_STYLUS2)
  n_button = GDK_BUTTON_SECONDARY;
else if (button == BTN_STYLUS3)
  n_button = 8; /* Back */
```

**Expected:** `BTN_STYLUS` arrives as `MOUSE_BUTTON_MIDDLE`, as it does for GTK applications, and `BTN_STYLUS3` as `MOUSE_BUTTON_XBUTTON1`. Then every barrel button is distinct from the tip.

**Seen in practice:** in a painting program built on Godot, the barrel button bound to "eyedropper while held" does nothing. Pressed while the pen hovers, it starts a left-button drag at pressure 0. The other barrel button works as a right click.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the project below with `--display-driver wayland` on a Wayland compositor, with a pen tablet whose pen has two barrel buttons.
2. Hover the pen over the window without touching, and press each barrel button in turn.
3. One button prints `BUTTON index=2` (right). The other prints `BUTTON index=1` (left), the same as touching the tablet with the tip.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

A project with nothing else in it. `project.godot` names `main.tscn` as the main scene, whose root is a `Control` (full rect) with this script:

```gdscript
extends Control

func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	var button := event as InputEventMouseButton
	if button != null:
		print("BUTTON index=%d pressed=%s" % [button.button_index, button.pressed])
	var motion := event as InputEventMouseMotion
	if motion != null and motion.button_mask != 0:
		print("MOTION mask=%d pressure=%.2f" % [motion.button_mask, motion.pressure])
```

Output with the pen hovering, pressing the barrel button that sends `BTN_STYLUS` and then the one that sends `BTN_STYLUS2`:

```text
BUTTON index=1 pressed=true
MOTION mask=1 pressure=0.00
BUTTON index=1 pressed=false
BUTTON index=2 pressed=true
MOTION mask=2 pressure=0.00
BUTTON index=2 pressed=false
```
